dataset: MIMIC-IV-ED demo v2.2 (ODbL v1.0, attribution required)
no_model_claims: No model was fitted and no model performance is reported. The open demo holds 222 ED stays; any accuracy figure from it would be meaningless and would be quoted later as though it were not.

proxy_wait.label: proxy wait (not true door-to-provider)
proxy_wait.notice: PROXY WAIT (NOT TRUE DOOR-TO-PROVIDER). `seen_time` was derived from a proxy timestamp because the source dataset records no first-provider-contact time. Every wait, every prolonged-wait label and every simulation KPI derived from it measures the proxy, not the door-to-provider interval the models were designed for. The two differ systematically, not merely noisily.
proxy_wait.proxy_used: first vitalsign charttime (usually recorded at triage, before a clinician)

first_pyxis_charttime.label: first pyxis charttime (a medication dispense, which follows a clinical decision and exists only for patients given a drug)

first_vitalsign_charttime.label: first vitalsign charttime (usually recorded at triage, before a clinician)

gap_between_proxies.reading: A positive gap means the medication dispense is later than the first vitals, which is the direction the schema predicts: vitals are taken at triage and a dispense follows a clinical decision. The median gap is the width of the disagreement between the two proxies, and any wait figure from either carries that much uncertainty about which interval it is measuring.

proxy_used.label: first vitalsign charttime (usually recorded at triage, before a clinician)

can_be_validated_on_mimic: The adapter and the column mapping, which is what this run demonstrates.
Per-patient features that use only that patient's own record: acuity, arrival mode, age, time of day, length of stay.
Disposition and acuity distributions, and the proxy-wait distribution, all labelled as proxy.
cannot_be_validated_on_mimic: Queue-state features (n_waiting, n_waiting_higher_priority, arrivals_last_1h and the rest). They are counts over concurrent patients, and concurrency does not survive per-patient date shifting.

The simulation's validation gate. It compares simulated against observed per-acuity mean and p90 wait, length of stay and abandonment for a department running as a queue -- which requires a real window of operation, not a patient sample.
The staffing search, which is scored by that simulation.
Door-to-provider wait itself. There is no first-provider-contact timestamp in MIMIC-IV-ED, with or without credentials.
reconstruction.date_shifting: MIMIC-IV shifts each patient's dates into a random future year, per patient, to de-identify them. Intervals inside one stay are preserved exactly -- arrival to departure is real -- but two patients' timestamps are not on a common clock.
reconstruction.note_on_full_access: Credentialed access to the full MIMIC-IV-ED removes the sample-size problem and nothing else on this list. The date shifting and the missing provider-contact timestamp are properties of the released data, not of the demo subset.
reconstruction.why: Because the shift is per patient, two stays that overlapped in reality do not overlap in the released data, and two that appear concurrent were probably years apart. Counting 'how many were waiting when this patient arrived' therefore counts an arbitrary set. The demo makes this visible in a second way: 0.01 stays per day across 32548 days is far below any real department's volume, because these are a sample of patients rather than a window of operation.

what_this_is: An adapter and mapping check against real data, plus a profile of what the tables contain.
